opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. Since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, full-time employees may have admin. Recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Anita Young (E001) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR states full_time, while Security DB states contractor with basic security training. Under the policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Since Anita requested admin (above the contractor maximum) and the security record indicates contractor/basic training, I grant the maximum permissible level: read. The conflicting full_time record is not sufficient to justify admin given the security database shows contractor status.
